Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

interpretation noun

an explanation of what something means

also interpret, misinterpret, take it the wrong way, take it as

classical

Cic. Off. 1.10 (by chapter): jūris (Lewis & Short)
Plin. NH 7.203: ostentōrum et somniōrum (Lewis & Short)

interpretātiō, interpretātiōnis f.

noun, third declension

explanation, interpretation

The explaining of laws, dreams, signs and words; also a translation (see translate).

Other words

  • interpretor, interpretārī, interpretātus sum — interpret, explain; understand (a thing in a certain way)

    verb, first conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 2.5: sī interpretārī velīs (Lewis & Short)

    From interpres, a go-between or interpreter: to explain, and also to take a thing in a certain sense (Lewis & Short).

  • accipiō, accipere, accēpī, acceptum — take (a remark) in a certain way

    verb, third conjugation, with in or ad + accusative · also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 606: ad contumēliam omnia accipiunt magis; Ter. Eun. 875: in eam partem accipiōque

    The everyday way of saying how something is understood: to take it as an insult, ad contumēliam accipere; in that sense, in eam partem.

Examples

  • Maledictum interpretandō faciās ācrius.

    Explain an insult and you make it sharper.Publil. Sent. M 23

  • nec quicquam aliud est philosophia, sī interpretārī velīs, quam studium sapientiae

    and philosophy, if you want to put it in other words, is nothing but the pursuit of wisdomCic. Off. 2.5 (Lewis & Short)

  • omnēs, quibus rēs sunt minus secundae, magis sunt nesciō quōmodo suspīciōsī; ad contumēliam omnia accipiunt magis

    all those whose affairs are going badly are somehow more suspicious; they take everything more as an insultTer. Ad. 605–606

See also explain, translate, mean, understand.

SourcesLewis & Short: interpretatio · Lewis & Short: interpretor · Lewis & Short: accipio
